reviewBasis.method: Single-reviewer static document/source/schema review; findings apply to plan statements and proposed joins, not executed behavior.
reviewBasis.designHeadDrift: Intervening commits only add unrelated F7 review artifacts; reviewed plan bytes unchanged.

r1FindingResolution.reason: The inventory now distinguishes accepted/application-selected contracts, current code, historical candidates and future successors. DR-125, DR-114, G20/G21, existing coded stderr and predecessor invocation-tag limitations are correctly acknowledged.
RequestId is universal; phase-specific identities, stored-Run correlation and the identity-allocation emergency are stated explicitly. No candidate/undetermined/ephemeral RunId is published.

The original free-text/regex safety claim is replaced with typed construction and per-sink classes; provider text and panic payloads are excluded, and OTLP has its own allowlist. Digest provenance/classification remains a non-blocking successor detail (OP-R2-NB-01), rather than a claim that a digest contains a literal source excerpt.
File writes are blocked on a named custody successor with original-owner predicates and retained handles; metadata and observation-only paths are nonpersistent and providers never receive log paths.

Recommended O1(a) uses existing channels and admitted host observations. O1(b) explicitly requires the common-control/compatibility successor, SDK/provider joins and qualification controls. Independent deadlines and liveness govern long phases.

Closed configuration and command/output successors are named; existing RequestId/diagnostics carriers are reused and no illegal StepTermination/DomainDetail fields are added. Outcome-affecting budgets are separated from operational settings.

Protocol faults, required-delivery faults and observability loss are separated, but the first cap row still misroutes discovery/output failures and the cancellation row confuses commit durability with invocation settlement.
Record/queue/ring admission, drop accounting and drain budgets are materially improved. The finite aggregate-retention overshoot and elapsed commit-wait bound are still unsupported.

The hook no longer allocates, symbolizes, takes logger/storage locks or attempts durable crash-file settlement. Blocking writes and inconsistent post-uncertainty effect claims remain; S-OP-7 names an owner but does not resolve those contradictions.

Advisory bytes/inodes, original-handle custody, earlier session effects and S-OP-8 are now named. Continuing after a failed observation on the same charged operation still contradicts the failure latch.

r1NonBlockingResolution.reason: M3 instrumentation precedes public timing surfaces; controls are authored at M3 and qualified later against product-v1 populations.
Statistics/start-end events/workloads and provisional defaults are named. The claimed hard wait bound remains OP-R2-03.
OTLP has explicit configuration/egress, its own allowlist and bounds, and is separated from required-delivery export; NB-02 asks for precise primary-outcome wording.
Bundle reads, consented output write, member classes and size bounds are separated.
Narrow APIs, audited exceptions and typed dispositions replace an informal no-swallow annotation.
Concurrency is automatic and recorded, with memory input; the zero-fit edge remains NB-04.
ADR count and fallback scope are corrected, and OpenSIP's signal exit remains 130 rather than inheriting predecessor 143.

requiredFindings.title: Separate discovery refusals and output failures from semantic Coverage exhaustion
requiredFindings.problem: The first matrix row still groups EVALUATION.WORK_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED, PROJECT.WORKSPACE_UNIT_LIMIT and OUTPUT.RENDERER_QUOTA_EXCEEDED as analysis caps that produce incomplete Coverage. PROJECT.WORKSPACE_UNIT_LIMIT is explicitly a UnitDiscoveryV1 refusal with REQUEST.UNSATISFIABLE, exit 2; it must not become an incomplete Run. Registration of OUTPUT.RENDERER_QUOTA_EXCEEDED as a DomainDetail code does not establish a Coverage route either. The selected required renderer has a delivery owner, including exit 4 and preservation of an already committed Run. Thus the statement that no D9/Coverage mapping change is proposed is not true of the written matrix.
requiredFindings.fix: Split this row by actual owning observation and lifecycle: discovery/admission refusal, semantic evaluation exhaustion, provider candidate/graph exhaustion under its exact protocol/Coverage join, and required/optional output failure. Name the existing code, termination class, exit and Run effect separately. Keep the evaluator's real Coverage exhaustion route; do not infer a route from a detail-code enum. Add proposed controls for workspace rejection before a Run and required-renderer failure with a retained Run.

evidence.note: Workspace-unit excess is REQUEST.UNSATISFIABLE / exit 2, never truncation.
Evaluation budget exhaustion has the indeterminate / COVERAGE.BUDGET_EXHAUSTED projection.
Renderer quota detail registration alone specifies no Coverage reduction.
Required projection/renderer failures have their own operational delivery route; committed RunId is retained.

requiredFindings.title: Keep commit durability separate from invocation settlement and cancellation projection
requiredFindings.problem: Row 263 applies 'never reclassified' after commit admission and says Committed keeps its class; §5.5 also says all signals map to 130 and that the settled commit outcome is reported unchanged. These statements conflate CommitOutcome with the invocation's D9 termination. X3D:170 explicitly keeps durability while sending Committed + latchedAfterAdmission through X7's DELIVERY.REQUIRED_FAILED / exit 4 row, with RunId and no delivery phase. CommitUndetermined projects as DURABILITY.COMMIT_FAILED / exit 4 with ExecutionId, not the D9 indeterminate class. The generic after-settle rule applies only once every required step is terminal, not merely after a Run commits. Attempt admission is also earlier than the final gate's evidence-COMMIT admission.
requiredFindings.fix: Write the cancellation join by precise phase and owner. Preserve the admitted evidence COMMIT's durability outcome, propagate the latch, and use X7's existing Committed-with-latch and CommitUndetermined projections. Distinguish attempt admission, FinalGate admission, commit return, required delivery and invocation settle. Retain the generic before-settle interrupt/after-settle unchanged rule where applicable; qualify the blanket 'all map to 130'. Controls must cover before final-gate admission, after that admission, after commit but before required-step settlement, and after complete invocation settlement.

evidence.note: Late latch preserves durability and expressly requires DELIVERY.REQUIRED_FAILED.
Committed with late latch and CommitUndetermined both have precise operational-failed exit-4 projections.
Settle means every required step is terminal; a pre-settle interruption can retain an earlier committed Run.
The unchanged-class rule is after-settle, not after commit admission.
FinalGate checkpoint admission immediately precedes permit.consume for evidence COMMIT.

requiredFindings.title: Do not claim an elapsed cancellation bound from the commit work budget
requiredFindings.problem: The lead judgment says a second-signal wait is bounded by the commit's own budget. The current budget counts objects, edges, bytes and records; it supplies no wall-clock deadline for each native operation. A finite number of charged operations does not bound time spent in a stalled native commit, barrier or I/O call. The broad interval from attempt admission to publish return includes more than the evidence-COMMIT critical section. The proposed p95 goal and reported maximum are measurements, not a proof of a hard wait bound.
requiredFindings.fix: Support deferral through the native effect already admitted, while withdrawing the unsupported elapsed-bound claim. Either state that this wait has no established wall-clock bound and make that limitation explicit in the cancellation goal, or name a reviewed platform/commit/supervision successor that supplies an actual time-bound mechanism and an honest timeout/process-death fate. Keep no further ordinary work after a latch, no invented clean refusal, no rewrite of committed or uncertain durability, and the X7 projection from OP-R2-02. Add a proposed stalled-native-operation/second-signal control; do not equate operation-count exhaustion with elapsed timeout.

evidence.note: Work limits are object/edge/byte/record counts, and Cost has no elapsed-time member.
Scopes enforce budget/failure closure, not native-call timeouts.
Uncertainty refuses further effects and preserves CommitUndetermined; it cannot be replaced by a timeout success/refusal.
Evidence COMMIT executes inside the admitted permit and returns a durability outcome.

requiredFindings.title: A failed capacity observation cannot leave the same operation ledger open
requiredFindings.problem: The plan charges fstatvfs to the admitted operation's work budget but then says a failed observation proceeds to commit with diagnostics. CommitSession::charge states that any failure latches that ledger and the caller stops with refused or undetermined. WorkLedger cannot be reopened by catching an error. X3D expressly rejects converting a native failure into a value to bypass this rule. A successful sample with no meaningful capacity figure can be advisory; a native, budget or custody failure on this operation cannot share that continuation.
requiredFindings.fix: Separate a successful 'capacity unavailable' observation from failed native I/O, custody/checkpoint or budget work. The former may disclose and continue; actual operation failures must latch and take the existing phase-specific stop/termination route. If advisory observation needs different authority, specify that as an explicit owner-reviewed S-OP-8 law change and show the allowed join; do not create a fresh ledger or wrap a failed syscall as successful 'unknown'. Add failed-observation controls, distinct from unknown-capacity and passing-sample/later-ENOSPC controls.

evidence.note: Every failed charged attempt step latches and requires stopping the session.
Catching nested failure cannot reopen an outer scope.
An unsuccessful scope latches on drop.
No ordinary work after failure; converting native failures to values is expressly rejected.

requiredFindings.title: The retention protocol does not establish its stated worst-case overshoot
requiredFindings.problem: The 512 MiB target is described as bounded best effort with overshoot limited to concurrent writers × 64 MiB plus crash files. But a skipped or failed pruning pass does not stop rotation or creation of another 64 MiB file. A single writer can retain N closed files across repeated busy-lock passes, or when deletion fails; its accumulated excess is not limited to one active file. Active-file locking prevents deletion of live files but does not bound this backlog. The parallel-writer control therefore promises a bound the specified protocol cannot enforce.
requiredFindings.fix: Either give an enforceable finite allowance for unpruned growth and stop/drop persistent logging when that allowance cannot be reclaimed, including lock-busy, deletion failure and abandoned-pruner cases, or explicitly withdraw the finite overshoot guarantee and describe the aggregate as an unbounded best-effort retention target. Keep each file's real hard cap and optional-loss outcome preservation. Align the response table, O2 and §10 control with the chosen claim. A shared reservation ledger is one option, not a requirement of this review.

evidence.note: Rotation remains permitted while a non-waiting pruning pass can be skipped; no retained-backlog admission rule is given.
Parallel-writer control asserts the stated overshoot.

requiredFindings.title: Make panic I/O bounds and post-uncertainty effects consistent
requiredFindings.problem: Removing allocation, locks and fsync improves the hook, but one short write is not a time bound. The unconditional first write to inherited fd 2 can block on a full pipe; append/no-follow also does not make a regular-file write nonblocking. Thus a panic can stall before the crash record or abort. Separately, line 280 allows two writes after a latched or uncertain operation, while the response table and crash control promise no further effect. Already-open descriptors do not themselves create an exception to X3D stopping.
requiredFindings.fix: Choose an honest panic policy for inherited blocking stderr and regular-file I/O. Use an independently justified bounded/nonblocking best-effort mechanism where available, skip unsafe writes, or explicitly state the elapsed limitation and remove contradictory no-deadlock/bounded claims. Do not treat O_NONBLOCK as a regular-file timeout. For a latched/uncertain operation, either suppress subsequent crash-file effects or explicitly propose the exact S-OP-7 exception with the X3D owner and revise the response and controls; never claim those writes already satisfy 'no further effect'. Add proposed full-stderr-pipe and stalled-file cases, alongside the existing logger-lock and ENOSPC cases.

evidence.note: Fixed stderr write precedes an append-file write, including after latching/uncertainty.
Uncertain operation refuses every further effect.
Uncertainty forfeits the only settlement reserve and admits no further effect.
Primary Linux manual: writing to a full blocking pipe waits for room.
Primary Linux manual: O_NONBLOCK does not prevent regular-file/block-device I/O from blocking.

nonBlockingObservations.title: Classify digests by provenance; hashing free text is not automatic privacy clearance
nonBlockingObservations.observation: Digests are a SafeField but have no explicit P0–P3 class. A SHA-256 of provider stderr/fault detail is a fingerprint of arbitrary private content and can permit candidate-value checks; a type named digest does not make its input P0. The existing test-output digest shape is a representation precedent, not a logging/export permission. This does not reopen the resolved prohibition on literal source excerpts.
nonBlockingObservations.recommendation: S-OP-2 should register digest provenance and sink class explicitly. Prefer counts/truncation by default for arbitrary text, or require the appropriate privacy class and consent for its digest. Never hash classified configuration secret values into report-bound members. Extend proposed canary controls to check forbidden derived fingerprints, not only plaintext.

evidence.note: Structural secret exclusion includes reader-usable hash oracles; outside free text remains disclosure-tier.

nonBlockingObservations.title: Optional export preserves the primary termination, which is not always success 0
nonBlockingObservations.observation: The statements 'optional export failure is success 0' and 'Export failure is success 0' quote a successful-primary golden too broadly. §5.2 correctly says optional observability loss never changes the outcome.
nonBlockingObservations.recommendation: Use 'does not change the primary termination/exit' consistently, including policy-failed, indeterminate, interrupted and operational-failed invocations. Keep WS:1378 as a success-case example, not the universal export-failure route.

evidence.note: Optional failure is disclosed and termination is unchanged.
The retained primary classes have distinct exits.

nonBlockingObservations.title: Name the storage-owned planned-size boundary for preflight
nonBlockingObservations.observation: The exact declared object set is built inside prepare_commit from ReplayedRun and the admitted session binding. It is not currently a value the host acquires just by sealing a Plan. The cited commit.rs:465 is a correct entry point, but does not itself expose the proposed preflight estimate.
nonBlockingObservations.recommendation: Have S-OP-8 specify an opaque storage-owned estimate or a charged planning/preflight phase after evaluation/replay and before admit_layout. Reuse the exact object plan and preserve reserve_end_path/ledger ordering; do not re-encode a second independent estimate in the host.

evidence.note: End-path reserve and charged object planning precede layout admission.

nonBlockingObservations.title: Define automatic concurrency when one provider does not fit
nonBlockingObservations.observation: The clamp floor of 1 overrides a memory-derived quotient of 0. As a proposed scheduling default it prevents zero workers, but it cannot also guarantee aggregate RSS headroom when a provider ceiling exceeds the available provider budget.
nonBlockingObservations.recommendation: S-OP-2/configuration/supervision work should define a zero-fit refusal or an explicitly admitted lower provider ceiling. Keep observed settings nonsemantic and measure concurrency with the host's own logging/RSS allowance included.

evidence.note: Logging allocation is charged to host RSS.
Provisional concurrency formula forces at least one provider.

O9.judgment: Support deferring restricted raw provider stderr capture beyond M3.
O9.reason: The no-text M3 path is simpler to enforce and consistent with private-source support. Counts, closed provider reason codes and carefully classified fingerprints can aid diagnosis without creating a raw-output archive. Revisit only through S-OP-9 and owner sign-off if measured support needs justify it.
O9.conditions: Any later capture must be separately classified and consented, bounded in bytes/age/retention, protected by admitted custody, excluded from ordinary logs/ring/default bundle/OTLP, and advertised as private untrusted text with honest redaction limits. A renamed SafeField or automatic bundle inclusion must not create consent.

cancellation.judgment: Support preserving an already-admitted commit's durability outcome; do not accept the stated bounded-wait claim or the written unchanged-D9 projection.
cancellation.reason: Commit work counters do not bound native elapsed time, and attempt admission does not mean invocation settlement. Preserve the FinalGate latch and X3D/X7 outcome joins; correct OP-R2-02/03 before accepting the plan.
